short: King of Scots from infancy, and the first man to rule both kingdoms.
full:
James became King of Scots at thirteen months, on his mother Mary's forced abdication in July 1567, and grew up under successive regents and a demanding Presbyterian tutor. By the 1590s he had established real authority in Scotland, curbing both the nobility and the kirk, and had set out his theory of kingship in The Trew Law of Free Monarchies.

Elizabeth I's death in March 1603 brought him the English and Irish thrones as well, joining the crowns in one person while the two kingdoms kept their own parliaments, churches and laws; his hopes of a full union were refused at Westminster. He survived the Gunpowder Plot of 1605, authorised the Bible translation published in 1611, promoted the plantation of Ulster, and kept England out of the Thirty Years War. He quarrelled repeatedly with parliaments over money and prerogative, and died in March 1625, leaving those arguments to his son.
